importance_ranking.reason: Buyers arrive with a defined site footprint, span requirement, eave height, and crane/insulation need — specs are the primary shortlisting gate. A listing without clear span, eave height, structure type, and crane provision cannot be evaluated and will be skipped.

High visual variation across sub-types (PEB gable vs single-slope vs multi-bay vs insulated panel shed) — buyers use the image to confirm the structural form and finish quality before reading specs. A photo of an actual erected shed signals execution capability, which is critical for a turnkey contract.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No single brand commands buyer recall across the Indian PEB market — buyers search by span, location, and execution track record, not manufacturer name; EPACK, Kirby, and Zamil are known to large EPC buyers but not to the SME majority.
importance_ranking.reason: This is a high-value turnkey contract — buyers evaluate manufacturer credentials, IS-code design compliance, erection experience, and post-erection warranty before committing. Seller identity is a primary trust signal, not a secondary qualifier.

Per-sq-ft price varies substantially with span, eave height, crane provision, and insulation type — buyers use listed price as a budget entry point after spec confirmation, not as a primary comparison signal. Final price is always project-quoted; listed price is indicative.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Supply-only contracts are quoted per MT; large lump-sum EPC orders are quoted per project. Per sq ft is dominant for turnkey DFSE contracts and must be shown to prevent confusion with per-MT or per-project quotes.
importance_ranking.reason: Per sq ft vs per MT vs per project are genuinely different billing bases — a buyer comparing listings cannot interpret price without knowing the unit. Unit ambiguity directly causes misquotation and buyer drop-off.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Span is the primary structural determinant — a 12 m span shed and a 30 m span shed require entirely different primary frame designs, steel tonnage, and foundation loads, making them non-interchangeable and driving the largest single price delta in this category.

Non-insulated vs PUF panel insulation defines a fundamentally different product tier — insulated sheds for temperature-controlled or pharma environments carry a significant cost premium and cannot be substituted with non-insulated structures for those applications.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Bay spacing (the longitudinal dimension of the shed) combined with clear span defines the total covered area and steel tonnage — sellers need this to size secondary members, purlins, and girts and to produce an accurate per-sq-ft quote.

IS:875 wind zone and IS:1893 seismic zone directly determine the design wind pressure and lateral load assumptions, which affect primary frame weight and cost — a Zone IV seismic design can add meaningful steel tonnage versus a Zone II design for the same span.
The number of bays multiplied by bay spacing gives the shed length — without this, sellers cannot determine total covered area or steel quantity, making accurate quotation impossible.

top_rfq_specs.reason: Total covered area is the single most important sizing input — it determines steel tonnage, project scope, and per-sq-ft quotation basis, allowing sellers to immediately assess whether the project is within their capacity and price range.
Clear span (width) is the primary structural design driver — sellers need this to determine primary frame configuration, column sizing, and whether the span is within their fabrication capability.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Pre-Engineered Building vs Conventional Steel Truss vs Pipe Shed defines the product tier, fabrication method, and cost band — sellers who only manufacture PEB cannot supply a conventional truss shed, making this a routing-critical requirement.

A shed with EOT crane runway beams requires reinforced columns, crane girders, and a different primary frame design — sellers need this upfront to determine structural feasibility and quote accurately.

Insulated sheds (PUF panel, rockwool, glasswool) for temperature-controlled or pharma environments are a fundamentally different product from non-insulated sheds — sellers need this to confirm product fit and price the insulation system.
